1.why: All screens show a static, clean layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary action buttons are solid dark blue and headings are prominent, though the persistent Logs panel competes for attention.

3.why: Top tabs (Request reset / Enter code / Sign in) and clear page titles make the main path easy to locate.

4.why: The flow requires remembering and transcribing long reset codes and a separate MFA code across multiple distinct steps.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill affordances, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: Apart from the email field retaining its value on the first page, there are no recognizable saved-item cues or familiar-account indicators.

7.why: Labels and instructions are generally short and readable, although the reset-code string itself is long and dense.

8.why: No error-message examples are shown; only success notices appear, so problem-and-fix guidance cannot be confirmed.

9.why: Password rules and ‘email-style contact’ guidance are given, but no concrete input examples (e.g., sample password) are displayed.

10.why: Only password + OTP is offered; no alternative methods such as face/biometric login are presented as clear choices.

11.why: Each screen presents essentially one primary task and one main button, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Green success messages (e.g., ‘reset instructions have been prepared’, ‘Security check complete’, ‘privacy conditions have been accepted’) explicitly state outcomes.

13.why: Safety notes and password-rule text provide some guidance, but contextual short tips for new steps are limited.

14.why: Forms remain available for re-entry after actions, yet no explicit ‘try again’ controls or inline recovery guidance are shown.

15.why: Header, tabs, card layout, button style and Logs panel stay identical across all 11 steps, giving a consistent design.
